points.why: It says the reviewer checks text against guidelines, cannot see the current UI, and that a stricter prompt is the same kind of check run harder.
It proposes a human or automated UI walkthrough of the steps and a release-to-article trigger that flags articles when referenced screens change.
It gates destructive or data operations behind a human or UI-verified check, but never names the agent-to-agent-to-publish path with no human and never recommends mapping who reviews what.
It recasts 98% as a measure of how rarely the reviewer objects, not of correctness, and notes it stays high on articles the reviewer can't verify.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly rejects the stricter prompt as the fix and offers structural alternatives.
